plugins/infrastructure/base.py:R3:BaseTr: hasattr(type(declared_schema), '__get__') is the descriptor-protocol test on a value read from cls.__dict__ of a class ELSPETH itself is creating (Tier 1, class-creation time). It does not probe for a missing attribute on data; it distinguishes the two authored shapes a subclass body can legally carry for input_schema — a plain schema value (moved into the property's backing store) versus a descriptor that deliberately overrides the property (left alone). Any descriptor kind (property, function, cached_property) is a legitimate override, so a nominal isinstance against one class would wrongly reject some of them; CPython itself decides descriptor-ness by exactly this type-level __get__ lookup. The site is classified approved-introspection in config/cicd/masquerade_baseline.yaml.
plugins/infrastructure/base.py:R5:BaseTr: isinstance(resolved, property) is a nominal check against the concrete builtin property class on the result of inspect.getattr_static over ELSPETH's own class hierarchy (Tier 1). It is itself the anti-shadowing guard for elspeth-d6eeb3a71d: if a mixin ahead of BaseTransform in the MRO shadows input_schema with a non-property, the check raises TypeError at class creation instead of letting undemoted models reach every row. The check is not defensive re-typing of trusted data — it is the assertion that fails closed; removing it deletes the control (masquerade baseline: 'do not remove this check').

isinstance(value, str) dispatches over the authored config VALUE of a column-naming option while scanning self.config.items(). The keys are selected by name (is_column_naming_config_option: field/fields/group_by/*_field/*_fields) across every registered plugin's config model, and those options are legitimately typed str (url_field), list[str] (keyword_filter.fields) or a str | list[str] union (group_by) depending on the model — the base class cannot name a single owned type per key. The check is a union dispatch over already-validated Tier-2 config values (the method runs right after config validation), not a shape guard hiding a contract violation; a value of another type is an option that names no column, and is skipped by design rather than crashed on.

isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) is the plural arm of the same union dispatch over an authored column-naming option value (str | list[str] | tuple across plugin config models, e.g. keyword_filter.fields, batch_data_quality_report.inspect_fields). It reads Tier-2 validated config; the base class cannot statically know which model type applies to a name-selected key, so the dispatch is by concrete builtin container class, not by structural probing. No error is masked: a non-sequence value simply names no column.

isinstance(item, str) filters the items of a plural column-naming option (list[str]) before recording provenance for each column name. Items are Tier-2 validated config values; the check pins that only a str can be a column name — a nested mapping or number inside a *_fields list (possible for options such as field_mapper.mapping-shaped values that share the naming suffix) is not a consumed column and must not be reported as one. This is nominal typing against the concrete builtin str, not a hasattr-style probe.

isinstance(value, str) dispatches over the value of a column-naming option read from the validated pydantic config model (Tier 2, via model_fields) or the raw config before validation. The same name-selected key (field/fields/*_field/*_fields/group_by) is typed str on some plugin models and list[str] on others (keyword_filter.fields, batch_data_quality_report.inspect_fields), so the base class dispatches by concrete builtin class to collect the column names each shape carries. Skipping the plural arm previously made every list-typed option invisible to demotion — the dispatch is the correctness fix, not a defensive guard.

isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) is the plural arm of the str | list[str] union dispatch over a validated column-naming option value (Tier 2). Plural options hold a list of column names; pydantic may hand back a list or a tuple depending on the model's annotation, so both concrete builtin container classes are named. This dispatch exists so demotion sees every column a plural option names; it does not mask a missing-attribute or wrong-shape bug.

isinstance(item, str) inside the plural arm keeps only str items of a list-typed column-naming option as column names (Tier-2 validated config). Options that share the *_fields naming suffix can carry non-str entries that are not column names; a column-name set must be str-only because it is unioned into consumed_input_fields and compared against schema field names. Nominal check against the concrete builtin str.
plugins/infrastructure/clients/http.py:R: isinstance(error, HTTPCallError) is a nominal check against HTTPCallError, a concrete dataclass ELSPETH defines in elspeth.contracts.call_data, on the error parameter typed CallPayload | None — a closed union of owned audit payload classes (Tier 1). _record_call is the shared audit persistence seam for every call kind; only the HTTP error variant carries a URL-bearing message that must be sanitized before it reaches the Landscape, so the branch selects the one member of the owned union that needs rewriting and passes every other variant through untouched. This is ADR-032 nominal typing of an owned type, not a shape guard over external data.
